B4b-01-atp-adp-cycle-schematic

Simple diagram of the ATP–ADP cycle. On the left, an ATP molecule drawn as an adenine shape (hexagon pair), a ribose pentagon, and three phosphate circles in a row. On the right, ADP with two phosphate circles and a separate single phosphate circle. A circular pair of arrows joins them: the top arrow (ADP + phosphate to ATP) fed by "energy from respiration" coming from a small mitochondrion icon, and the bottom arrow (ATP to ADP + phosphate) giving out "energy for cell work" with small icons for a muscle, a dividing cell and a protein chain.
B4b-02-glycolysis-pathway-flowchart

Simple flow diagram of glycolysis drawn inside a pale cytoplasm-coloured box. At the top, a chain of six circles representing glucose (6C). An arrow shows 2 ATP being used to give a 6C sugar phosphate (six circles with a small phosphate tag at each end). This splits into two chains of three circles (triose phosphate). Each then passes down an arrow giving off NADH and 2 ATP, ending as pyruvic acid (three circles) at the bottom. On the right side, a tally box shows "ATP used: 2", "ATP made: 4", "net gain: 2 ATP".
B4b-07-oxygen-deficit-exercise-line

Line graph of oxygen consumption against time for a person before, during and after a short period of vigorous exercise. The horizontal axis shows time in minutes with three marked zones (rest, exercise, recovery); the vertical axis shows oxygen uptake. The line is low and flat at rest, rises during exercise to a plateau, then falls gradually back to the resting level during recovery. A shaded area at the start of exercise (where uptake lags behind need) is marked as the oxygen deficit, and the shaded area under the curve during recovery above the resting level is marked as the oxygen debt. A dashed line shows the oxygen actually needed during exercise above the plateau.
B4b-04-mitochondrion-electron-transport-chain

Cut-away drawing of a mitochondrion showing the outer membrane, the folded inner membrane (cristae) and the matrix. An enlarged inset of one crista shows a row of carrier proteins in the membrane with NADH and FADH₂ handing over hydrogen at the start, a wavy arrow of electrons passing from carrier to carrier, small ATP symbols being produced along the chain, and at the end oxygen joining with hydrogen to form water.
B4b-09-exhaled-air-limewater-breathing

Two boiling tubes of lime water side by side, connected by T-shaped glass tubing to a single mouthpiece held by a student. Tube A (left): air enters from outside through a long tube dipping into the lime water and leaves through a short tube to the mouthpiece; lime water clear. Tube B (right): air from the mouthpiece passes down a long tube into the lime water and out through a short tube; lime water milky. Small arrows show the direction of air flow when breathing in (through A) and breathing out (through B).
B4b-10-germinating-seeds-heat-production

Two vacuum flasks side by side, each clamped upside down on a stand, with a thermometer passing through a cotton wool plug into the flask among seeds. Flask A contains germinating bean seeds with small shoots and roots; its thermometer reads higher (red level higher). Flask B contains shrivelled boiled seeds; its thermometer reads lower. A small note shows the starting temperatures as equal.
B4b-12-yeast-anaerobic-fermentation-experiment

Fermentation experiment with two set-ups side by side in a beaker of warm water with a thermometer. Each set-up is a boiling tube containing a cloudy yeast and sugar mixture with a thin yellow layer of oil on top, closed with a bung carrying a delivery tube that dips into a test tube of lime water. Left (experiment): bubbles rising in the mixture and in the lime water, which is milky. Right (control: boiled yeast): no bubbles, lime water clear.
B4b-13-yeast-industrial-fermentation-products

An illustrated panel of everyday products made with yeast, arranged around a central drawing of oval budding yeast cells: a loaf of bread and a bowl of puff-puff, a bottle of beer and a calabash of burukutu, a gourd of palm wine beside an oil palm tree with a tapping container, a bottle of ethanol fuel beside cassava roots and sugarcane, a jar of yeast extract with a "B" vitamin symbol, and a bag of animal feed. A small separate corner shows a mouth with white patches representing thrush, marked as harmful.
B4b-03-krebs-citric-acid-cycle

Circular diagram of the Krebs cycle inside a pale mitochondrion matrix shape. Acetyl CoA (two circles) enters at the top and joins oxaloacetic acid (four circles) to form citric acid (six circles). Arrows go round the circle clockwise: citric acid (6C) to a 5C acid with CO₂ and NADH leaving; 5C to 4C with a second CO₂ and NADH leaving; then through 4C acids with ATP, FADH₂ and NADH leaving; back to oxaloacetic acid. Above the cycle, pyruvic acid (3C) from glycolysis is shown changing to acetyl CoA (2C) with CO₂ and NADH leaving (link reaction). Small outward arrows for CO₂ coloured grey, NADH and FADH₂ coloured orange, and ATP coloured green.
B4b-05-aerobic-cellular-respiration-overview

Overview flow diagram of the whole of aerobic respiration in a cell. On the left, a cell's cytoplasm with glucose entering and glycolysis producing 2 pyruvic acid, 2 ATP and 2 NADH. An arrow leads into a large mitochondrion on the right, showing the link reaction (pyruvic acid to acetyl CoA, releasing CO₂), the Krebs cycle as a circle in the matrix (releasing CO₂, NADH, FADH₂ and 2 ATP), and the electron transport chain on the cristae, where oxygen enters and water leaves and many ATP (34) are produced. A total box at the bottom reads the sum.
B4b-06-pyruvic-acid-fate-branching

Branching flow diagram of the fate of pyruvic acid. At the top, glucose in the cytoplasm changing to 2 pyruvic acid by glycolysis with "2 ATP" beside the arrow. Three branches lead down: left branch "with oxygen" going into a mitochondrion to give carbon dioxide and water and many ATP; middle branch "no oxygen: yeast and plants" giving ethanol and carbon dioxide (small yeast cell icon); right branch "no oxygen: animal muscle" giving lactic acid (small muscle icon).
B4b-08-plant-respiration-carbon-dioxide

Experimental set-up to show that carbon dioxide is produced in respiration, drawn left to right: air entering a flask of potassium hydroxide solution through a tube that dips into the liquid; a delivery tube to a flask of clear lime water; a delivery tube to a bell jar on a glass plate covered with a dark cloth, containing a small potted plant (its pot wrapped in polythene); a delivery tube to a flask of milky lime water; and finally a tube to an aspirator (a large bottle with a tap releasing water). Arrows show the direction of air flow.
B4b-11-simple-respirometer-germinating-seeds

Simple respirometer set-up shown as two boiling tubes side by side in a water bath. Each tube has potassium hydroxide solution at the bottom, a wire gauze platform above it, and a rubber bung with a bent capillary tube leading to a horizontal scale with a drop of coloured liquid (index). The experimental tube contains germinating seeds on the gauze; its index has moved towards the tube (arrow). The control tube contains glass beads; its index has not moved.
